characters.raw: Shri Gajanan Maharaj (श्री गजानन महाराज / समर्थ / सिद्धयोगी): Central saint. Ovis 70–83 address his unknown origin and devotional interpretation of his appearance; 88–144 describe the first meeting, food and the non-dual teaching. His arrival is not identified as his birth.
characters.name: Shri Gajanan Maharaj
characters.description: Central saint. Ovis 70–83 address his unknown origin and devotional interpretation of his appearance; 88–144 describe the first meeting, food and the non-dual teaching. His arrival is not identified as his birth.

characters.raw: Bankatlal Agarwal (बंकटलाल आगरवाल): First observer and questioner; recognizes his mistaken first impression, asks for a meal and praises the good fortune of Shegaon (Ovis 97–122, 132).
characters.name: Bankatlal Agarwal
characters.description: First observer and questioner; recognizes his mistaken first impression, asks for a meal and praises the good fortune of Shegaon (Ovis 97–122, 132).

characters.raw: Damodarpant Kulkarni (दामोदरपंत कुलकर्णी): Bankatlal’s companion; offers Maharaj water, brings it in a gadva, and hears the teaching about distinctions (Ovis 98, 126, 133–143). The speaker of Ovis 136–137 is inferred from Ovi 135, not explicitly named in those two verses.
characters.name: Damodarpant Kulkarni
characters.description: Bankatlal’s companion; offers Maharaj water, brings it in a gadva, and hears the teaching about distinctions (Ovis 98, 126, 133–143). The speaker of Ovis 136–137 is inferred from Ovi 135, not explicitly named in those two verses.

characters.raw: Devidas (देविदास / देविदासबुवा): Devout householder associated with the Paturkar lineage and Madhyandina branch; described as mathadhipati in Ovi 85. A son’s ritushanti meal occasions the scene (84–87).
characters.name: Devidas
characters.description: Devout householder associated with the Paturkar lineage and Madhyandina branch; described as mathadhipati in Ovi 85. A son’s ritushanti meal occasions the scene (84–87).

characters.raw: Sant Dasganu Maharaj (संत दासगणू): Poet and narrator, requesting divine and saintly inspiration in the opening ovis and introducing the Shegaon story (1–69, 145–146).
characters.name: Sant Dasganu Maharaj
characters.description: Poet and narrator, requesting divine and saintly inspiration in the opening ovis and introducing the Shegaon story (1–69, 145–146).

characters.raw: Lord Ganapati / Saraswati / Pandurang / Shiva / Devi / Dattatreya: Invoked by the poet in the opening prayers; they are invocations, not additional characters participating in the Shegaon encounter (1–29).
characters.name: Lord Ganapati / Saraswati / Pandurang / Shiva / Devi / Dattatreya
characters.description: Invoked by the poet in the opening prayers; they are invocations, not additional characters participating in the Shegaon encounter (1–29).

characters.raw: Ramchandra Patil (रामचंद्र पाटील): Requested the poet to recount Maharaj’s life during a Kartiki pilgrimage to Pandharpur (66–68).
characters.name: Ramchandra Patil
characters.description: Requested the poet to recount Maharaj’s life during a Kartiki pilgrimage to Pandharpur (66–68).

characters.raw: Arjuna and Subhadra (अर्जुन / सुभद्रा): Used in Bankatlal’s analogy for seeking liberation; not present in the Shegaon event (120–121).
characters.name: Arjuna and Subhadra
characters.description: Used in Bankatlal’s analogy for seeking liberation; not present in the Shegaon event (120–121).

locations.raw: Shegaon (शेगाव): Town in Varhad, placed in Khamgaon taluka in the poet’s account; setting of Maharaj’s appearance and the first meeting (58–64, 74, 83–144).
locations.name: Shegaon
locations.description: Town in Varhad, placed in Khamgaon taluka in the poet’s account; setting of Maharaj’s appearance and the first meeting (58–64, 74, 83–144).

locations.raw: Devidas’s house and road (देविदासांचे घर / रस्ता): The house hosting the ritushanti meal and the road outside where discarded leaf plates lay (84–96, 113–118).
locations.name: Devidas’s house and road
locations.description: The house hosting the ritushanti meal and the road outside where discarded leaf plates lay (84–96, 113–118).

locations.raw: Well and cattle watering trough (कूप / हाळ): The hal beside a well is explicitly a cattle-drinking trough, not a stream or river (134–140).
locations.name: Well and cattle watering trough
locations.description: The hal beside a well is explicitly a cattle-drinking trough, not a stream or river (134–140).

locations.raw: Pandharpur and Akot (पंढरपूर / अकोट): Places mentioned in the poet’s account of the book’s creation; not part of the first Shegaon meeting (56, 66).
locations.name: Pandharpur and Akot
locations.description: Places mentioned in the poet’s account of the book’s creation; not part of the first Shegaon meeting (56, 66).

locations.raw: Sajjangad (सज्जनगड): An alleged origin named as hearsay in Ovi 75; Ovi 76 says strong evidence is lacking. Do not present it as established fact.
locations.name: Sajjangad
locations.description: An alleged origin named as hearsay in Ovi 75; Ovi 76 says strong evidence is lacking. Do not present it as established fact.

objects.raw: ओवी / चरण (Ovi / Charan): Four-part Marathi verse form; the chapter contains 146 ovis in the transcriptions checked.
objects.name: ओवी / चरण
objects.description: Four-part Marathi verse form; the chapter contains 146 ovis in the transcriptions checked.

objects.raw: माघ वद्य सप्तमी / शके १८००: The lunar day and Shaka year in Ovis 74 and 83. The verse does not state a Gregorian date or Maharaj’s birth date.
objects.name: माघ वद्य सप्तमी / शके १८००
objects.description: The lunar day and Shaka year in Ovis 74 and 83. The verse does not state a Gregorian date or Maharaj’s birth date.

objects.raw: ऋतुशांती (Ritushanti): A traditional family rite for Devidas’s son, with a prepared feast in the household (86).
objects.name: ऋतुशांती
objects.description: A traditional family rite for Devidas’s son, with a prepared feast in the household (86).

objects.raw: उष्ट्या पत्रावळी / शीत (Used leaf plates / rice grain): Discarded leaf plates and individual grains of food; central to the teaching on अन्नपरब्रह्म (87, 93–96).
objects.name: उष्ट्या पत्रावळी / शीत
objects.description: Discarded leaf plates and individual grains of food; central to the teaching on अन्नपरब्रह्म (87, 93–96).

objects.raw: बंडी / दिगंबर (Bandi / Digambar): Ovi 88 mentions an old bandi while 92 calls his form digambar. Preserve the separate source descriptions rather than resolving them into a new physical claim.
objects.name: बंडी / दिगंबर
objects.description: Ovi 88 mentions an old bandi while 92 calls his form digambar. Preserve the separate source descriptions rather than resolving them into a new physical claim.

objects.raw: भोपळा / तुंबा (Gourd water vessel): A gourd for drinking water, referred to again when Bankatlal offers to arrange water (89, 125–131).
objects.name: भोपळा / तुंबा
objects.description: A gourd for drinking water, referred to again when Bankatlal offers to arrange water (89, 125–131).

objects.raw: कच्ची चिलीम (Unbaked clay chilim): Maharaj’s self-made clay pipe, explicitly described as unfired (90).
objects.name: कच्ची चिलीम
objects.description: Maharaj’s self-made clay pipe, explicitly described as unfired (90).

objects.raw: गडवा / हाळ (Gadva / Hal): A water vessel carried by Damodarpant, and an animal-watering trough beside the well (134–137).
objects.name: गडवा / हाळ
objects.description: A water vessel carried by Damodarpant, and an animal-watering trough beside the well (134–137).

objects.raw: वाळा (Vetiver / Khus): A fragrant root used to scent the water brought in a gadva (137); the speaker is contextually inferred as Damodarpant from Ovi 135.
objects.name: वाळा
objects.description: A fragrant root used to scent the water brought in a gadva (137); the speaker is contextually inferred as Damodarpant from Ovi 135.

objects.raw: अन्नं ब्रह्मेति / गुळवणी / निरिच्छा: The Upanishadic food teaching (94–95), the named sweet preparation gulavani as an analogy (116), and desirelessness portrayed as Maharaj’s estate (122).
objects.name: अन्नं ब्रह्मेति / गुळवणी / निरिच्छा
objects.description: The Upanishadic food teaching (94–95), the named sweet preparation gulavani as an analogy (116), and desirelessness portrayed as Maharaj’s estate (122).
